bosc:provenance.subject: Findlay's PUBLIC places — the three civic/flood land holdings the Blanchard River story walks, Hancock County OH (FIPS 39063), 26 parcels / 1,921.77 ac county-CAMA: the Maumee Watershed Conservancy District's EAGLE CREEK DRY STORAGE BASIN acquisition (18 parcels, 795.35 ac, Eagle Township), the City of Findlay WATER POLLUTION CONTROL CENTER at 1201 S River Rd (2 parcels, 77.85 ac) and the City's UPGROUND RESERVOIR holding on TR 207/205 (6 parcels, 1,048.57 ac, Marion Township). #1462, sub-issue of #1265. Deliberately a SEPARATE file from parcel-assemblage.geojson — see caveats.
bosc:provenance.source: OGRIP — Ohio Statewide Parcels Public View (owner ogrip_agol), FeatureServer layer 0, scoped County='Hancock', read through the ohio_parcels connector (OHIO_STATEWIDE_PARCEL_SCHEMA). Waterbody names/areas cross-checked against the USGS NHD Waterbody - Large Scale layer; township attribution against the Census TIGER county-subdivision layer.
caveats: ⚠️ THIS FILE IS NOT THE SITE'S CAMPUS AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED TO ONE. `SiteProfile.parcels_relpath` points at parcel-assemblage.geojson (the One Power / One Energy holding) and nothing else, because that path drives the `geo/campus` map feed, the SSURGO dominant-HSG sample and the stormwater screen's total area. Folding 1,921 ac of reservoir, WWTP and flood-basin ground into it would draw public infrastructure as 'campus', sample soils 13 km from the hub, and inflate a runoff denominator. These are the site's other PLACES; they are committed as evidence and read by citation.

⚠️ SAME 2023-05-08 VINTAGE AS THE HUB FILE. The OGRIP Hancock slice carries CurrentTo 2023-05-08. For these three holdings that matters less than it does for the hub — a conservancy district and a municipal water system do not turn over — but the Eagle Creek acquisition was still in progress when this export was cut, so 795.35 ac is a FLOOR on what MWCD holds today, not a closing figure.

⚠️ THE OGRIP LAYER SERVES ONE ROW PER POLYGON PART, NOT ONE ROW PER PARCEL. Five of these 26 parcels come back as 2-4 separate rows (the Wood-County CAMA shape, #1436); each is merged here into a single MultiPolygon feature and `geometry_parts` records how many rows it took. Deduping the query result by parcel id — the obvious defensive move — silently DROPS real geometry: it would have cost this file 220 ac.

THE 765-ACRE IMPOUNDMENT AND THE 795-ACRE HOLDING ARE DIFFERENT MEASUREMENTS. hancockcountyflooding.com publishes 'approximately 765 acres' for the Eagle Creek Dry Storage Basin — the area WITHIN THE DAM ALIGNMENT that the impoundment floods. This file carries 795.35 CAMA ac / 782.77 planar ac of LAND ACQUIRED, in three non-contiguous blocks. Acquired land properly exceeds the impoundment (embankment, access, buffer), so the two are consistent — but they are not the same number and neither is derived from the other. THE DAM ALIGNMENT ITSELF IS STILL [open]: no surveyed impoundment polygon or ODNR Dam Safety permit exhibit is in the corpus, so nothing here is the basin outline. See data/extracted/findlay/flood/eagle-creek-basin-footprint.handoff.yaml.

THE PUBLISHED VERBAL BOUNDS CHECK OUT, AND SO DOES THE CREEK. The handoff records the basin as bounded west by TR 76 and east by US-68 in Eagle Township, ~4 mi south of downtown Findlay; #1462's own issue text quotes 'west of U.S. 68 and just north of Township Road 49'. The 18 MWCD parcels carry situs addresses on exactly those four roads (TR 76, TR 77, TR 49, US RT 68); their POLYGON extent spans 40.9681-40.9902 N and their parcel CENTROIDS 40.9738-40.9890 N, against downtown Findlay at 41.0440 — 3.0-4.6 mi south by polygon extent, 3.4-4.5 by centroid. (Quote whichever you mean: the centroid span is what reads as the published '~4 miles south', the polygon extent is the committed geometry's actual bounds.) The USGS NHD large-scale flowline layer puts seven Eagle Creek segments through the block. Township confirmed via Census TIGER. [verified]

THE WPCC PARCEL CONTAINS THE PERMITTED OUTFALL — a point-in-polygon test, [verified]. The profile's cited outfall 2PD00008001 (Blanchard River RM 56.42, 41.049722/-83.667778, Ohio EPA fact sheet 2PD00008*UD p.7) falls inside parcel 610000926490, situs 1201 S River Rd. `contains_wpcc_outfall` records the test. The adjoining 27.33-ac city parcel 610000926560 ('0 RIVER RD') is carried as the second wwtp-role feature on ADJACENCY and common ownership only — no instrument in the corpus assigns it to the plant, so read it as city land next to the WPCC, not as plant land.

⚠️ THE WPCC PARCEL'S GEOMETRY UNDER-COVERS ITS DEEDED ACREAGE BY 21%. 610000926490 reads 50.52 ac in CAMA but its three polygon parts measure 39.758 ac planar — a 10.76-ac, -21.3% gap, the largest in the file. It is NOT a lone outlier, and the spread it sits in is worth reading before trusting any single planar figure here: 200001032776 is -17.5% (3.25 ac CAMA -> 2.68 planar), and the other 24 parcels run -7.2% to +5.2%. Two readings fit that spread and this file does not choose between them: served geometry that under-covers the deed (a missing part, a river-bounded edge, a stale split), or CAMA acreages never re-surveyed. Either way cite 50.52 ac as the deeded figure and do NOT use this polygon as a plant-area measurement.

THE TWO RESERVOIRS ARE NAMED BY NHD, NOT BY THE PARCEL LAYER. The parcel rows say only 'CITY OF FINDLAY' on TR 207 / TR 205 in Marion Township. The USGS NHD Waterbody - Large Scale layer carries exactly two reservoirs (FType 436) over this block: 'Findlay Reservoir' at 177.9 ac and 'Findlay Upground Reservoir Number Two' at 628.9 ac — 806.8 ac of WATER SURFACE inside 1,048.57 ac of city LAND. Which parcel underlies which reservoir is NOT asserted: the parcel boundaries and the waterbody boundaries are different geometries from different producers and were not reconciled. ⚠️ This is the same Findlay Reservoir whose diversion and low-flow augmentation release make USGS gage 04189000 a REGULATED station — the defect that retired the derived 8.67 cfs 7Q10 for the WPCC reach in #1458.

acres is the county CAMA (auditor) figure from the OGRIP LandArea column; planar_acres is measured from this geometry in UTM 17N (EPSG:32617). The two are NOT reconciled and neither is adjusted to the other.

THERE IS NO OWNER FIELD HERE, AND THE PROPERTY NAMES SAY SO. The OGRIP public view is owner-redacted (owner_field=''), so this file carries `owner_mailing_name` — the recipient line of the tax-bill mailing label, trailing city/ZIP stripped — and NOT an `owner` or `owner_of_record` property, because a tax-bill recipient is not the same thing as an owner of record. `owner_mailing_address` carries the label verbatim. Note the conservancy district's label is truncated inconsistently by the source itself — some rows read 'MAUMEE WATERSHED CONSERVANCY', others 'MAUMEE WATERSHED CONSERVANCY DISTRICT'; both are the same entity and neither is corrected here.
Right-county guard: Hancock County OHIO (FIPS 39063). Tax-district prefixes are '20' (Eagle Township), '33' (Marion Township) and '61' (City of Findlay).
